Em português o futuro muda a terminação: In English the future is made with "will" ("I will read") or "going to" ("I'm going to read"). Russian has TWO forms of the future, depending on the aspect. The first is the compound future, of the imperfective: «буду» + imperfective infinitive = I will do / I will be doing (process, habit, duration). The verb «быть» in the future: я буду, ты будешь, он будет, мы будем, вы будете, они будут. The verb that follows always stays in the infinitive.
o português diz «vou ler» ou «lerei». «Б: English says "I will read", which looks a lot like this: «буду» works like "will be", followed by the infinitive. «Буду читать» is like "I will be reading" (for a while, regularly).
«Буду» is not used with a perfective verb.
Diga: «Завтра я буду работать. Я буду до: Say: «Завтра я буду работать. Я буду дома. Мы будем обедать в кафе.»
O perfectivo se conjuga com as mesmas te: The perfective is conjugated with the same endings as the present (1st or 2nd conjugation), but the meaning is FUTURE: the action has not been done yet and will be completed. Прочитать → я прочитаю, ты прочитаешь, он прочитает, мы прочитаем, вы прочитаете, они прочитают. Verbs with a prefix follow the pattern of the base verb: писать → напишу (с → ш), смотреть → посмотрю. Some pairs change the root and the consonant mutates: купить → куплю (п → пл), ответить → отвечу (т → ч), сказать → скажу. And «дать» is irregular: дам, дашь, даст, дадим, дадите, дадут. «Буду» is never used with the perfective.
em português o futuro dos verbos de ação: in English the future of a completed action is "I will read it" or "I'll finish reading it". Russian uses the perfective, conjugated as if it were the present.
Tomorrow I will read the book (to the end).
